title: Arcade Prep Rush
premise: A neon arcade chef catches valuable falling ingredients and avoids harmful junk to build a virtual shift total before running out of lives.
interaction_model: Single-screen real-time pointer/touch control; the player moves the chef horizontally to collect good drops and avoid bad ones.
objective: Earn the highest possible virtual cash total by catching good ingredients, preserving lives, and sustaining a streak of successful catches.
progression: Arcade score-attack run structure with increasing pressure through continuous spawning, soft combo rewards, a low-life warning, and instant restart after game over.
theme: Retro-futurist kitchen arcade with neon colors, playful food iconography, and exaggerated game-show energy.
mood: Fast, colorful, snackable, upbeat, and lightly chaotic with celebratory feedback on success and harsh but playful punishment on mistakes.
likely_audience: players who enjoy simple reflex and collection games
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core design is a catch-and-dodge arcade game with a chef skin rather than a systems-heavy cooking simulator.
High confidence in the score, lives, combo-feedback, and restart loop because they are explicit in code.
Medium confidence on intended mastery curve because there are no authored levels or late-game rule changes; difficulty mainly comes from continuous random spawns.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished browser game called "Arcade Prep Rush," a single-screen neon kitchen arcade experience where a cartoon chef stands near the bottom of the screen and the player moves that chef left and right using mouse, pointer, or touch input to catch good falling ingredients while avoiding harmful junk. Present the game as a fast score-attack shift: tomatoes, cheese, and steak should fall from the top and award different virtual cash amounts when caught, while hazards like bombs or rotten food should remove lives on contact. Start the player with 3 lives, show a HUD with a money total and remaining hearts, and end the run when all lives are lost, then reveal a game-over panel with the final prep total and a restart button. Use a requestAnimationFrame-style loop, smooth horizontal following toward the pointer position, random falling item spawns, particle bursts, floating score text, screen shake on mistakes, and a lightweight combo system that rewards several successful catches in a row with extra celebratory feedback without needing deep stat progression. Make the presentation vivid and arcade-like: dark purple neon background, glowing UI pills, retro fonts, animated reward and fail reactions, and upbeat audio with start, collect, bonus, fail, warning, and game-over cues. Keep the experience accessible, mobile-safe, instantly replayable, and clearly virtual in its money language so it feels like an energetic casual catch-and-dodge web game rather than a realistic cooking sim.
